summary: The article provides a generally accurate and well-explained overview of debt funds, duration, and investment strategies in a rising interest rate environment, but contains one significant inaccuracy regarding the taxation of debt funds for investments made after April 1, 2023.

claims.claim: For instance, if a bond has a Macaulay Duration of 5 years, its price is expected to fall by approximately 5% for every 1% (100 basis points) increase in interest rates.
claims.note: This statement incorrectly attributes price sensitivity directly to Macaulay Duration. Modified Duration is the measure that approximates the percentage change in a bond's price for a 1% change in yield. While Macaulay Duration is related to Modified Duration, they are distinct concepts. A Modified Duration of 5 would imply a 5% price change for a 1% yield change, but Macaulay Duration itself is a measure of time (weighted-average time until cash flows are received).

claims.claim: Categories like Ultra Short Duration, Low Duration, and Short Duration funds fall under this umbrella as per SEBI's classification.
claims.note: SEBI classifies debt funds into various categories including Ultra Short Duration (Macaulay duration 3-6 months), Low Duration (Macaulay duration 6-12 months), and Short Duration (Macaulay duration 1-3 years).

claims.claim: Categories like Medium to Long Duration, Long Duration, and Gilt funds with a 10-year constant duration fall into this group.
claims.note: SEBI's classification of debt funds includes Medium to Long Duration (Macaulay duration 4-7 years), Long Duration (Macaulay duration more than 7 years), and Gilt Fund with 10-year constant duration.

claims.claim: When interest rates are on an upward trajectory, short-duration debt funds become more attractive. Their lower interest rate sensitivity means their NAVs are less impacted by rising yields compared to long-duration funds.
claims.note: Short-duration funds are indeed less sensitive to interest rate changes due to their shorter Macaulay duration, making them generally more suitable in a rising interest rate environment.

claims.claim: For investments held for up to 36 months, gains are treated as short-term capital gains and added to your income, taxed at your slab rate. For investments held over 36 months, gains are treated as long-term capital gains and taxed at 20% with indexation benefit.
claims.note: This information is outdated. For debt mutual fund investments made on or after April 1, 2023, all gains are treated as short-term capital gains and taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate, regardless of the holding period. The benefit of long-term capital gains with indexation for debt funds has been removed for new investments.

article_title: Navigating Debt Funds: Short vs. Long Duration as Rates Rise
